ops.title: daemonkit's own docs claim detached spawn is load-bearing — it has not been true for a year
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the P4.1 Q7 detachment check. This is a documentation defect with a security
consequence, which is why it is P1 rather than P3.

`README.md:44` says:

> "A daemon that owns kernel state — a FUSE mount, a keychain session — can't ride its parent's
> lifetime. Spawn it detached … and the resource survives the CLI, the terminal, and the login
> session that started it. **fusekit's mount holder has run this way in production since day one**"

`doc.go:2` ("detached spawn") and `CHANGELOG.md:866` ("proc: detached spawning …") carry the same
claim. It has not been true since fusekit's holder became a launchd-registered signed app
(fusekit/holder/plan.go:494 — "Agent returns a detached desired LaunchAgent", where "detached" means
*launchd job*, not detached fork; registered via cc-pool/internal/statusapp/hooks.go:201-207).

The audit found the opposite invariant is what ships: fusekit's holder TEARS DOWN the mount when it
exits (holder/native_process.go:266-307 — Stop, awaitUnbound, awaitSettlement), a prior-generation
survivor is a *liability the next generation kills* rather than a child it adopts
(holder/process_recovery.go:205-222 refuses admission while any receipt remains), and cookiesync's
so-called "detached" ssh child is the inverse of detachment — the origin holds the child's stdin
open for its whole life so the peer reaps when this side dies (internal/bridge/keepalive.go:29-32).

Why it matters beyond accuracy: phase 4 freezes `Cmd`/`Channel`/`Owned` with **no** detachment
primitive, because the child-side handoff authentication is `creds.pid == os.Getppid()`
(internal/proc/handoff.go:68) — a detached child reparents to launchd, getppid() returns 1, and the
check fails. The relaxation an implementer reaches for is `creds.uid == os.Getuid()`, which makes any
same-UID process that can plant a descriptor at fd 3 an acceptable "parent". This stale prose is the
only artifact in the repo that would make a future reader believe detachment is load-bearing and go
looking for that relaxation.

The changelog entry is historical record — correct it with a line in the next release entry rather
than rewriting the shipped one. README.md and doc.go get rewritten outright.

ops.text: README.md:44, doc.go:2, and the changelog narrative no longer claim fusekit's mount holder runs detached in production
The replacement text points at the launchd package + deploy's sealed activation as the supported way to outlive a CLI
